Its importance to Chapter 3 is not the test for a technology issue, and no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition names it.

Full alignment with the data protection rules is central to the data theme and is repeated by the Commission in 2023, 2024 and 2025, but none of the 2020 to 2025 reports names it in the key recommendations, and it is in no benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition. The 2024 and 2025 main findings record no progress, but that is a finding and not a key recommendation, so this is a central requirement with thin support under the test. National and agency items were not counted.

The Commission has raised the Agency's dependence and capacity from 2021 to 2025 and an independent authority is central to the data theme, but the requirement appears only in body text, in 2023 and 2025 and in the 2025 communication in general terms. It is in no key recommendation, benchmark or Reform Agenda payment condition, and the main findings do not mention it, so it is a central requirement with thin support, on the same footing as RI-TEC-019.

The mechanisms are legal alignment and implementing rules, led by one ministry with the regulator and parliament, and a new law and amendments were adopted in 2025, which favours progress. Against that, the Commission assessed the Reform Agenda step as not achieved in both 2025 and 2026, with gaps remaining in two laws, and the by-laws are described as technically demanding and were not yet due. Adoption has been quick but alignment has twice fallen short, which does not support High.
